full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite- parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 31-7-2002 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge and SCC Judge, Raozan Chittagong in SCC Suit No. 2 of 1997 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 5. After hearing the parties and on an appraisal of the evidence and materials on record and in the facts and circumstances of the case, the lower Court decreed the suit on the observation, inter alia, that the plaintiff-opposite parties succeeded in proving their case. 

 6. As against the judgment and decree of the Court of first instance, the defendant-petitioners have preferred the instant Civil Revision and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. The only point for determination in this Rule is, whether the impugned judgment and decree passed by the SCC Judge are according to law? 

 8. At the outset, Mr MA Jalil, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioners, submits that in view of the evidence and materials on record, the bonafide requirement of the suit shop house by the plaintiff-opposite parties has not been proved and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court are not according to law and that being so, it calls for interference from this Revisional Court. 

 11. On the contrary, Mr ASM Kamal Amroohi Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite-parties, submits that it is in the cross-examination of the DW 1 SM Nasiruddin that the defendant-petitioners are defaulters and the bonafide requirement of the suit shop house by the opposite-parties has been legally proved on evidence and such being the position, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the SCC Judge are very much in accordance with law and so no exception can be taken thereto. 

 15. A reference to the impugned judgment of the Court below positively shows that on the grounds of default and bona fide requirement of the suit shop house, it decreed the suit in favour of the opposite-parties. In this regard, Mr MA Jalil has seriously assailed the finding of bonafide requirement of the suit shop house on the part of the opposite-parties on the score that it is in the cross-examination of the PW 1 Abu Musa Siddique that the plaintiff-opposite-parties have another shop house at Fakirhat in front of Raozan Police Station and that the opposite-party Nos. 2 and 3 live abroad and the opposite-party No. 1 is the Imam of a mosque. 

 32. Accordingly, the Rule is disposed or without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the SCC Judge are affirmed with the modifications mentioned in the body of this judgment.
